title: Garmin Autoland engages after a King Air B200 loses cabin pressure at 23,000 ft and lands it at Broomfield, Colorado, in its first real emergency use
summary: On 20 Dec 2025 Garmin Autoland flew a depressurised King Air B200 to a landing at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport; two pilots unhurt.
account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. with two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 ft it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization; when cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically, sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control and flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. The crew chose to leave it engaged. Nobody was treated; the FAA said it was investigating and the NTSB that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency.
purpose: Autoland exists to take complete control of an aircraft and land it when the pilot cannot fly, engaging on its own when cabin altitude exceeds a set level; that is what happened here, although the two pilots turned out not to be incapacitated and chose to let it finish.
taxonomy_note: Occupant and aircraft safety is not among the six types; Organizational Efficiency is chosen, as for the crash-avoidance record, because the operator resolved an in-flight emergency with its crew and aircraft intact and without emergency treatment.

ratings.reason: Two pilots who had lost cabin pressure at 23,000 ft were on the ground in Broomfield within about 35 minutes of departure, untreated and uninjured; because they were conscious and could have flown the descent themselves, the benefit is a safe automatic recovery, not a documented life saved.
Buffalo River Aviation's aircraft 'landed safely without incident', in the airport spokeswoman's words; no damage is reported, and the FAA investigation was still open.

ai_role.statement: Autoland engaged itself when cabin altitude exceeded the limit, declared the emergency to controllers with automated 'pilot incapacitation' broadcasts, and flew the descent, approach and landing; the pilots elected to leave it engaged rather than take over, so the landing is the system's work but the counterfactual, that they could not have landed, is not established. Garmin, the FAA and the operator all call it an automated system; none calls it AI. It is here because the OECD Monitor lists it as an AI system, and The Register describes it choosing landing sites from runway length, distance and fuel range.

produced_by: An aircraft fitted with Garmin Autoland; Garmin says more than 1,700 are equipped.
A rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization that pushed cabin altitude past the system's automatic trigger.
A crew that decided to let the automatic sequence run to touchdown rather than take over.
must_hold: The aircraft remains airworthy: Autoland is a fail-safe for a working aircraft whose pilot cannot fly it, in the words of the journalist CBS quoted.
A suitable airport is in range; The Register describes selection by runway length, distance and fuel range.
Controllers and ground services act on the automated broadcasts, as Broomfield's two fire departments did.

headline: Garmin Autoland lands depressurised King Air B200; pilots unhurt

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and six news reports. The Monitor dates the event 22 December 2025; every report puts the landing on Saturday 20 December, which is used here. Early reports (AVweb, Denver7, ABC's headline) said the pilot was incapacitated; the operator's CEO, quoted by CBS, ABC and The Register, says the system engaged on cabin-altitude exceedance and the crew were not incapacitated. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented because the crew were conscious and elected to leave the system engaged, so no counterfactual is established. Aircraft type is given as Super King Air 200 (ABC, Denver7) and King Air B200 (AVweb, The Register). The Monitor's General Aviation News and FOX31 follow-up links returned HTTP 403, AVweb's 'crew decision' piece returned 404, and the Independent blocked fetching, so its Yahoo syndication is cited. Garmin's Autonomí pages returned only navigation, so no vendor source is cited; Garmin's statements are quoted via the news reports.
